name: Islamophobia Advisory Council
description:
The council focuses on raising awareness about Islamophobia, promoting inclusivity, and creating a safe environment for all. Through workshops, training sessions, and collaborative events, we aim to combat stereotypes, encourage dialogue, and support our diverse Muslim community, ensuring that every individual feels valued and respected on campus.

Convened by the Office of Inclusive Excellence (Del Norte Hall, Room 2004).

name: College Assistance Migrant Program (CAMP)
description: The College Assistance Migrant Program (CAMP) is a federally funded program designed to serve students from migrant and seasonal farm working backgrounds succeed at Sacramento State. CAMP facilitates the transition from high school to college and offers first-year support services to develop skills necessary to persist and graduate from college in a timely manner.

name: College & Department Scholarships
description: The Scholarships Office at Sacramento State is dedicated to supporting students by offering a wide variety of institutional and community scholarships. The Scholarships Office awards nearly $4 million dollars in institutional scholarships each year.

name: Dreamer Resource Center
description: The DRC provides guidance, assistance, resources and knowledge to those looking to support and learn more about the culture, heritage, and life of our immigrant and undocumented students and community members.

name: Career Center
description: Through a collaborative career development approach, we engage, educate and empower our students and alumni to thrive and successfully contribute to our community, economy and future workforce. We develop employer and community partnerships to recruit, collaborate with and inform our talented students and alumni.

name: El Centro Serna
description: El Serna Center is dedicated to cultivating an environment that champions leadership, empowerment, self-advocacy, and civic engagement among those interested in culture, heritage, and life of Chicanx/Latinx students and those from other under-represented backgrounds at Sacramento State University.

name: Associated Students, Inc. (ASI)
description: The Associated Students provides support to a variety of programs aimed at meeting the needs of the students of the University. The Association also serves as a vehicle for participation in the governance of the University.

name: Women's Resource Center (WRC)
description: The WRC cultivates a safe space where students can be empowered and affirmed. We provide various services to all students interested in learning about and supporting women-identifying students and allies. Our programming challenges sexism, socialized gender roles, and the patriarchy. We also focus on gender identity issues and offer a platform for discussions with a feminist lens.

name: Pride Center
description: The Pride Center provides students looking for a connection to campus with programs and events, access to resources on campus and in the community, a welcoming space, and opportunities for education about LGBTQIA communities and the intersections of many identities and experiences.

name: Disability Access Center (DAC)
description: The DAC offers support to any enrolled student who meets the standard of a qualified individual with a disability (QID), whether temporarily or permanently disabled. It strives to foster that a disability is a positive identity, and set up students for a path of independence and self-advocacy.

name: Peer & Academic Resource Center
description: PARC's mission is to promote the scholastic achievements of students through enriched and supportive peer-learning opportunities that aid students along the pathway to degree attainment. PARC utilizes a relatively untapped resource at the University, the talented and knowledgeable students who serve as SI Leaders, Peer Advisors and Peer Tutors.

name: Student Employment Office
description: As part of the Office of Human Resources, the Student Employment Office is dedicated to helping enhance student learning by providing meaningful work experiences on campus and ensuring that students get the most out of their employment experiences throughout their time at Sacramento State.

name: Student Technology Programs and Services
description:
The mission of the Student Technology Center is to teach students the technology needed to complete their coursework and collaborate with faculty on the use of technology in courses.

Services: Assistance creating and practicing presentations, workshops, 1-on-1 training of software products, large document printing, and group project support.

name: Student Financial Services Center
description: The Student Financial Services Center is comprised of 20 dedicated staff members providing cashiering, disbursement, billing, collections and refund services (Registration, Parking, and Housing Fees; Refunds; Check Disbursements; One Card).

name: Center on Race, Immigration & Social Justice (CRISJ)
description: The Center on Race, Immigration and Social Justice (CRISJ) addresses social and educational inequities facing the university and larger community. It seeks to transform the educational culture to an exciting and empowering one that reflects the strengths and needs of our local and diversified communities.

name: Basic Needs Resource Center (BNRC)
description:
Whether you need groceries, clothes, toiletries, parenting supplies, or a couch surfing kit, everything at the BNRC is free and just for Sac State students. No barriers. No judgment. Just confidential support when you need it.

Visits are appointment-based, and students can shop the pantry up to once a week.

name: Muslim Student Association (MSA)
description: The Muslim Student Association at Sacramento State University stands to provide a safe, inclusive space for Muslims, and Non-Muslims, on campus and beyond. We strive to educate about Islam, counter misconceptions about the religion, and propagate Islam with utmost clarity.

name: Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP)
description: The purpose of this organization is to bring awareness and activism for the occupation in Palestine. We are an advocacy group of students, faculty, and community members at CSU Sacramento devoted to the liberation of Palestine, promoting justice and human rights.

name: Afghan Students Association
description:
The purpose of this organization is to promote, embrace and celebrate Afghan culture through raising awareness, promoting social events, as well as fundraising.

The association also helps impoverished communities in Afghanistan by raising money, clothing, and school supplies, and hosts social events that build connections among Afghan students at Sacramento State.

name: Pakistani Student Association
description: To familiarize Pakistani students with Sacramento State while introducing the campus to the Pakistani culture and building a community on campus.

name: Arab Student Union
description: A club to bring together the Arab community here at Sacramento State to celebrate and enhance our culture and heritage. All who are passionate about the purpose/mission of the organization are welcomed regardless of identity.

name: Iraqi Student Association
description:
The Iraqi Student Association is the Sacramento State student organization for Iraqi students and anyone interested in Iraqi culture and heritage.

Join or contact the group through the campus club directory (search for "Iraqi"), and follow the association on Instagram at @Iraqistudentasso.
